TRUST-02.reason: Perimetr owns no SSH/SFTP client or host key store. Its remote transports are HTTPS and signed Agent callbacks.

PERM-04.reason: Perimetr consumes the Updater socket and creates only service-owned state. Shared socket directory ownership belongs to the host helper.

HLT-07.reason: Perimetr does not implement remote storage. Backup downloads are local operator copies with a separately escrowed recovery secret.

INT-04.reason: Perimetr does not enroll scheduled backup pipelines. Agent assignment uniqueness is covered separately by domain regression tests.

INT-09.reason: Perimetr exposes a browser operator interface and typed Agent capabilities; it does not provide a chat command gateway or bot menu.

INT-10.reason: Perimetr does not register external provider webhooks. Machine callbacks use its own signed Agent and Pod protocols.

INT-11.reason: No external provider webhook worker, repository filter or import queue belongs to this service. Signed domain callbacks have separate tests.

DATA-03.reason: Perimetr has bounded request-local ZIP uploads, with no resumable remote storage upload sessions or quota reservations.

DATA-05.reason: This service owns no external storage credentials or namespace. Recovery is verified by an isolated database restore drill.

DATA-07.reason: No shared remote storage root exists in the Perimetr profile. Its persistent database and state are private Compose volumes.

DATA-08.reason: Perimetr has no automatic remote backup producer. No export credentials or automatic backup agent are provisioned.

DATA-09.reason: No automatic backup scheduler is approved for Perimetr in the current central service profile; Neptune is not installed or exposed.

DATA-10.reason: Independent operator backup storage and failure domains are deployment choices outside this local application; no redundancy is claimed.
